RFC2966-2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-09-30. Forbidden: an L1L2 router originating an L2-derived prefix in its L1 LSP with bit 8 of the default metric clear. The earlier gap (no unit read bit 8 of a narrow TLV 128/130 entry) is closed: root TestRFC2966NarrowLeakUpDownBit feeds applyLeak an L2->L1 internal and external narrow leak, decodes fragment 0 of the originated L1 LSP, and requires the raw default-metric octet of 10.2/24 in TLV 128 and 10.3/24 in TLV 130 to carry 0x80 with the 6-bit metric intact (positive); the L1-derived 10.1/24 leaked into L2 goes out in TLV 128 with bit 8 clear (negative). The chain is complete: spf TestISISLeakOriginationL1L2 proves leakInto sets UpDown only for the L2->L1 direction, TestISISEngineLeakOrigination carries it through the engine on TLV 135, and the new unit proves the narrow wire encoding. Recorded + on lsdb/encode.go narrowIPReachEntryBytes and +/- on lsdb_wiring.go leakedToPrefixInfos.

RFC2966-2-2.note: Unchanged on re-read: TestISISLeakOriginationL1L2 gained only the RFC5305-4.1-1 tag comments. Forbidden behaviour: re-advertising into L2 a prefix learned via L1 with the up/down bit set. TestISISLeakOriginationL1L2 assertion 3 (hasPrefix(leak.IntoL2, alreadyDown) -> t.Errorf) goes red if leakInto stops skipping p.UpDown; the negative keeps a clear-bit L1 prefix leaking up (assertion 1), so a blanket drop also goes red. Both polarities in the one unit.

RFC2966-2-3.note: Forbidden behaviour: an L1L2 router advertising back into L2 an L2->L1 inter-area route it learned via L1. TestISISLeakFixpoint round 2 re-injects the leaked-down prefix as an L1 advertisement with UpDown set and fails on hasPrefix(r2.IntoL2, l2Derived); round 1 (negative) requires the same L2 prefix to leak down, so suppressing all leaking goes red too.

RFC2966-3.2-1.note: Forbidden: a less preferred class selected for a lower metric, or two members of one class ranked against each other. TestRFC2966EveryClassMemberOutranksNextClass drives every member of each class the fixture can express (L1 internal and external-with-internal-metric; L2 internal and external-with-internal-metric, which is also the L1->L2 inter-area member to the receiver; L2->L1 internal and external-with-internal-metric; L1 external-metric; L2 external-metric; L2->L1 external-metric) against every member of the next class, preferred one at cost 100/metric 60 against 1/1. TestRFC2966EqualClassMembersCompareByMetric requires the lower metric to win between two members of one class in both orders, so a member ranked apart from its class goes red. Recorded red on preferenceRank and better; the older adjacent-pair tests remain.

RFC2966-x-1.note: Forbidden behaviour: accepting an IP Internal Reachability (TLV 128) prefix whose metric-type bit says external. TestRFC2966InvalidInternalExternalMetricExcluded sets bit 0x40 on the TLV 128 entry of the cheaper route and requires metricWinner to pick the dearer valid route (id 2, 160); clearing the bit requires the cheap route back (id 3, 2), so both an accept-anyway and a drop-everything implementation go red.
